sentences.en: I'm Christopher Johnson, filling in this week for Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是克里斯托弗·约翰逊，本周代班罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In the mid-1970s, the national media was reporting on the rise of a new socioeconomic group
sentences.zh: 20世纪70年代中期，全国媒体都在报道一个新兴社会经济群体的崛起，

sentences.en: that was quickly gaining unprecedented access to jobs, education, backyard swimming pools, the good life.
sentences.zh: 他们迅速获得了前所未有的工作、教育、后院游泳池和美好生活的机会。

sentences.en: Journalists seemed fixated on what many were calling the, quote, new Black middle class.
sentences.zh: 记者们似乎专注于许多人所称的“新黑人中产阶级”。

sentences.en: Black families have entered the mainstream of American life in larger numbers than ever before in our history.
sentences.zh: 黑人家庭以前所未有的规模进入了美国生活的主流。

sentences.en: No one of them is exceptional, but their total story is.
sentences.zh: 他们中的每一个人都不算特别，但他们的整体故事却非同寻常。

sentences.en: The media's obsession at the time was with how, for this one section of Black America,
sentences.zh: 当时媒体痴迷于这样一个话题：对于这部分黑人美国人来说，

sentences.en: the protests and violence of the 1960s seemed to be cross-fading into quiet middle class achievement.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代的抗议和暴力似乎正在淡出，转而走向平静的中产阶级成就。

sentences.en: Nowhere near as exciting as a riot or a burning is the move into middle-income America,
sentences.zh: 向中等收入美国人的转变远没有骚乱或纵火那样令人兴奋，

sentences.en: but this is what Black Americans are achieving more than ever before.
sentences.zh: 但这正是黑人美国人比以往任何时候都更努力实现的成就。

sentences.en: In August 1973, Ebony Magazine had its own special issue all about the Black middle class.
sentences.zh: 1973年8月，《乌木》杂志出版了一期关于黑人中产阶级的特刊。

sentences.en: On the cover, there was a fisheye photo of an anonymous Black man wearing a crisp suit
sentences.zh: 封面上是一张鱼眼镜头拍摄的照片，照片中一个不知名的黑人男子穿着挺括的西装，

sentences.en: with a tight afro and a briefcase walking through the city with purpose.
sentences.zh: 留着紧致的爆炸头，提着公文包，目标明确地走在城市里。

sentences.en: The stars of the moment were regular, ascendant Black Americans.
sentences.zh: 那一刻的主角是普通、正在崛起的黑人美国人。

sentences.en: We were dealing with people that were having economic stability for the first time in generations.
sentences.zh: 我们面对的是几代人以来第一次获得经济稳定的人们。

sentences.en: This is writer and cultural critic Craig Seymour.
sentences.zh: 这位是作家兼文化评论家克雷格·西摩。

sentences.en: Although there'd always been some version of the Black middle class,
sentences.zh: 虽然黑人中产阶级一直存在某种形式，

sentences.en: Craig says this group of Black Americans was different.
sentences.zh: 但克雷格说，这群黑人美国人与众不同。

sentences.en: The Black middle class of the 70s was really reaching the world with arms wide open
sentences.zh: 70年代的黑人中产阶级确实张开双臂拥抱世界，

sentences.en: and trying to have new opportunities and new experiences
sentences.zh: 并试图获得新的机会和新的体验，

sentences.en: that have just not been afforded to masses of Black people before that.
sentences.zh: 这些机会和体验在之前从未向广大黑人群众开放过。

sentences.en: And as these new masses were figuring out what upward mobility felt like,
sentences.zh: 当这些新群体在感受向上流动的滋味时，

sentences.en: they were also exploring what Black middle classness sounded like.
sentences.zh: 他们也在探索黑人中产阶级听起来是什么样的。

sentences.en: It was the aspiration to expand, to seek out new type of sounds,
sentences.zh: 这是一种渴望扩张、寻求新类型声音的愿望，

sentences.en: kind of have new sonic adventures.
sentences.zh: 算是一种新的声音冒险。

sentences.en: That's the type of thing that was so different.
sentences.zh: 这就是如此与众不同的地方。

sentences.en: In the previous decade, some of the biggest songs in Black popular music
sentences.zh: 在过去十年里，黑人流行音乐中一些最热门的歌曲

sentences.en: had been dancey, sometimes political, and heavy on the funk.
sentences.zh: 都是节奏感强、有时带有政治色彩且充满放克风格的音乐。

sentences.en: Like James Brown's Black Power anthem,
sentences.zh: 比如詹姆斯·布朗的黑人权力赞歌，

sentences.en: Say It Loud, I'm Black and I'm Proud.
sentences.zh: 《大声说出来，我是黑人，我引以为傲》。

sentences.en: This song was a good time with a strong message.
sentences.zh: 这首歌既好听又传达了强有力的信息。

sentences.en: But by the mid-1970s, that new generation of Black Americans
sentences.zh: 但到了70年代中期，那一代新的黑人美国人

sentences.en: was gravitating to a much more mellow sound,
sentences.zh: 开始转向一种更柔和的声音，

sentences.en: a sound that matched the soft life of their middle class dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 一种与他们中产阶级梦想中的安逸生活相匹配的声音。

sentences.en: They wanted music that was smooth and easy,
sentences.zh: 他们想要平滑、轻松的音乐，

sentences.en: and all about love and romance.
sentences.zh: 而且全是关于爱与浪漫的。

sentences.en: And at a small Black college radio station in Washington, D.C.,
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿特区的一家小型黑人大学广播电台，

sentences.en: a show called The Quiet Storm would give them exactly what they were looking for.
sentences.zh: 一个名为《宁静风暴》的节目正好满足了他们的需求。

sentences.en: Four hours of my favorite songs presented for your enjoyment.
sentences.zh: 四个小时我最喜欢的歌曲，为您呈现。

sentences.en: Relax and enjoy The Quiet Storm.
sentences.zh: 放松心情，享受《宁静风暴》。

sentences.en: The concept of The Quiet Storm radio show was pretty straightforward.
sentences.zh: 《宁静风暴》广播节目的概念非常简单直接。

sentences.en: An evening program featuring hours of mostly uninterrupted,
sentences.zh: 一个晚间节目，播放数小时几乎不间断的、

sentences.en: That simple format made The Quiet Storm an overnight sensation.
sentences.zh: 这种简单的形式使《宁静风暴》一夜成名。

sentences.en: And as the show became a fixture in homes and on car stereos throughout Black D.C.,
sentences.zh: 随着该节目成为华盛顿特区黑人家庭和汽车音响里的常客，

sentences.en: it also set off a debate over how Black music should sound and what it should say.
sentences.zh: 它也引发了一场关于黑人音乐应该听起来怎样以及应该表达什么的辩论。

sentences.en: In the early 1970s, before The Quiet Storm radio show was created,
sentences.zh: 在20世纪70年代初，《宁静风暴》广播节目诞生之前，

sentences.en: was an epicenter of Black middle class life.
sentences.zh: 是黑人中产阶级生活的中心。

sentences.en: The city was experiencing new levels of Black access to good jobs and higher education.
sentences.zh: 这座城市正在经历黑人获得好工作和高等教育的新阶段。

sentences.en: was nicknamed the Chocolate City, a town full of Black socialites, politicians, and professionals.
sentences.zh: 被称为“巧克力之城”，是一个充满黑人名流、政客和专业人士的城镇。

sentences.en: You had affluent, middle class Black folks that liked to go out and party, that had homes.
sentences.zh: 你有富裕的中产阶级黑人，他们喜欢出去聚会，有自己的房子。

sentences.en: It was a thriving community of all kinds of socioeconomic, but Black.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满各种社会经济背景但都是黑人的繁荣社区。
非常、非常纯粹的黑人社区。
我们当时正处于繁荣时期。

sentences.en: And then the mecca of all the HBCUs, Howard University.
sentences.zh: 还有所有历史黑人大学（HBCU）的麦加——霍华德大学。

sentences.en: Howard got a new radio station in 1971 and renamed it with its own call letters,
sentences.zh: 霍华德大学在1971年拥有了一个新的广播电台，并以其呼号重新命名，

sentences.en: WHUR, which stood for Howard University Radio.
sentences.zh: WHUR，代表霍华德大学广播电台。

sentences.en: This was the first Black-owned radio station in D.C.,
sentences.zh: 这是华盛顿特区第一家由黑人拥有的广播电台，

sentences.en: a city where three out of four residents were Black.
sentences.zh: 在这个城市，四分之三的居民是黑人。

sentences.en: Even though WHUR was technically a commercial outlet, it had a strong grassroots feel.
sentences.zh: 尽管WHUR在技术上是一家商业电台，但它有着浓厚的草根气息。

sentences.en: There was a news department, blocks of cultural programming, and lots of music.
sentences.zh: 它有新闻部、大块的文化节目和大量的音乐。

sentences.en: And not just the up-tempo R&B or funky dance music you might hear on other stations,
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是你可能在其他电台听到的快节奏R&B或时髦的舞曲，

sentences.en: but also Roots reggae, Chicago blues, and freedom songs.
sentences.zh: 还有根源雷鬼、芝加哥蓝调和自由之歌。

sentences.en: Deanna Williams was one of WHUR's first DJs.
sentences.zh: 迪安娜·威廉姆斯是WHUR的第一批DJ之一。

sentences.en: She had a show called Ebony MoonbeaMs.
sentences.zh: 她有一个节目叫《乌木月光》。

sentences.en: I would come on, you know, this is Deanna Williams, Ebony Moonbeams on 96.3 WHUR,
sentences.zh: 我会上台，你知道，我是迪安娜·威廉姆斯，96.3 WHUR的《乌木月光》，

sentences.en: and tonight I've got some special things for you.
sentences.zh: 今晚我为你准备了一些特别的东西。

sentences.en: Like the other DJs, Deanna had eclectic tastes,
sentences.zh: 像其他DJ一样，迪安娜有着兼收并蓄的品味，

sentences.en: and the freedom to play mostly whatever she wanted.
sentences.zh: 并且有自由去播放她想放的任何音乐。

sentences.en: You heard the beauty of us.
sentences.zh: 你听到了属于我们的美。

sentences.en: 360 degrees of the Black experience is what we did.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的是360度全方位的黑人体验。

sentences.en: But this kind of programming was not bringing in a lot of money.
sentences.zh: 但这种节目并没有带来多少钱。

sentences.en: So just a few years after WHUR first went on the air,

sentences.zh: 霍华德大学校长詹姆斯·奇克，

sentences.en: started pushing the station to focus more on raising revenue.
sentences.zh: 开始推动电台更多地关注增加收入。

sentences.en: Management had a new mandate, which, as one historian put it,
sentences.zh: 管理层有了新的任务，正如一位历史学家所说，

sentences.en: was to pursue an upscale commercial niche in the FM market.
sentences.zh: 要在调频市场追求一个高端的商业利基市场。

sentences.en: Basically, they wanted a more bougie audience.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们想要更小资的听众。

sentences.en: Dr. Cheek offered me the opportunity to first become the sales manager
sentences.zh: 奇克博士给了我机会，让我先成为销售经理，
负责霍华德大学广播电台WHUR。

sentences.en: As part of that new mission, WHUR hired a woman named Kathy Hughes.
sentences.zh: 作为新使命的一部分，WHUR聘请了一位名叫凯西·休斯的女士。

sentences.en: Here's Kathy in an interview with KUT Radio in 2020.
sentences.zh: 这是凯西在2020年接受KUT电台采访时的片段。

sentences.en: I was blessed my first year.
Increased the ratings and the revenue substantially.
sentences.zh: 收视率和收入都大幅增长。

sentences.en: In 1975, when Kathy was just 28 years old,
she became the first woman to run a broadcast facility in the nation's capital.
sentences.zh: 她成为了国家首都第一位管理广播设施的女性。

sentences.en: And she would soon reshape the station in ways that would ripple
sentences.zh: 她很快将以一种在未来十年里影响黑人音乐和广播的方式，

sentences.en: through Black music and radio for the next decade.
She did it by focusing on a new target audience,
sentences.zh: 她通过专注于一个新的目标受众做到了这一点，

sentences.en: D.C.'s young, thriving Black middle class.
sentences.zh: 即华盛顿特区年轻、繁荣的黑人中产阶级。

sentences.en: Kathy Hughes was incredibly savvy about understanding how radio audiences worked,
sentences.zh: 凯西·休斯在理解广播受众如何运作方面非常有头脑，

sentences.en: how to sell airtime, but also how to program certain types of music to specific audiences.
sentences.zh: 不仅懂得如何销售广告时间，还懂得如何为特定受众编排特定类型的音乐。

sentences.en: Music critic Eric Harvey has written about WHUR's history.
sentences.zh: 音乐评论家埃里克·哈维曾撰文讲述WHUR的历史。

sentences.en: And he says, as Kathy was thinking about how to make music shows
sentences.zh: 他说，当凯西在思考如何制作音乐节目

sentences.en: to attract new listeners to the station,
sentences.zh: 以吸引新听众到电台时，

sentences.en: she decided to survey the people closest to her.
sentences.zh: 她决定调查她身边的人。

sentences.en: You know, she was looking at her girlfriends.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她观察了她的女性朋友们。

sentences.en: Who was she hanging out with?
Upwardly mobile, single Black women who were being completely underserved by popular radio.
sentences.zh: 那些向上流动的单身黑人女性，她们在流行广播中完全被忽视了。

sentences.en: From her focus group, Kathy realized that a local show that appealed to single Black women,
sentences.zh: 通过焦点小组，凯西意识到一个吸引单身黑人女性的本地节目，

sentences.en: especially professional Black women, could be really popular and a great source of ad revenue.
sentences.zh: 尤其是职业黑人女性，可能会非常受欢迎，并成为广告收入的巨大来源。

sentences.en: Kathy began to loosely conceive of a weekend evening show focused on romantic music,
sentences.zh: 凯西开始构思一个周末晚间节目，专注于浪漫音乐、

sentences.en: slow, soulful R&B ballads, and very smooth love songs.
sentences.zh: 缓慢、深情的R&B民谣和非常柔和的情歌。

sentences.en: She knew that there were a lot of single, young Black women in the D.C.
sentences.zh: 她知道华盛顿特区有很多年轻的单身黑人女性。

sentences.en: This is writer and cultural critic Craig Seymour again.
sentences.zh: 这是作家兼文化评论家克雷格·西摩再次发言。

sentences.en: So she thought, well, hey, who doesn't want to be serenaded?
sentences.zh: 所以她想，嘿，谁不想被小夜曲打动呢？

sentences.en: You know, who doesn't want to have somebody play love songs to them
sentences.zh: 你知道，谁不想有人为他们播放情歌，

sentences.en: and talk in a deep voice and listen to that?
sentences.zh: 用低沉的声音说话，然后静静聆听呢？

sentences.en: So she kind of tailored the show to that particular audience.
sentences.zh: 所以她为那个特定的受众量身定制了这个节目。

sentences.en: One version of the show's origin story, and there are a few,
sentences.zh: 关于这个节目起源的故事有几个版本，

sentences.en: is that Kathy had a bit of a tough time finding the right DJ to host the show.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是凯西在寻找合适的主持人时遇到了一些困难。

sentences.en: She eventually settled on an intern named Melvin Lindsey, who also babysat her son.
sentences.zh: 她最终选定了一位名叫梅尔文·林赛的实习生，他当时还负责照看她的儿子。

sentences.en: Although Melvin was not Kathy's first or favorite choice for the DJ gig,
sentences.zh: 虽然梅尔文并不是凯西最初或最喜欢的DJ人选，

sentences.en: he was the one who would soon take her idea and make it a huge success.
sentences.zh: 但他很快就采纳了她的想法并取得了巨大的成功。

sentences.en: Melvin was a handsome, button-down kid from D.C.,
sentences.zh: 梅尔文是一个来自华盛顿特区的英俊、穿着考究的孩子，

sentences.en: known for carrying a briefcase around campus.
sentences.zh: 以在校园里随身携带公文包而闻名。

sentences.en: He could also be super shy.
Deanna Williams was one of Melvin's mentors at WHUR.
sentences.zh: 迪安娜·威廉姆斯是梅尔文在WHUR的导师之一。

sentences.en: Melvin was still a student when I was on the radio.
sentences.zh: 我在电台工作时，梅尔文还是个学生。

sentences.en: He was very quiet until he got comfortable.
sentences.zh: 在感到自在之前，他非常安静。

sentences.en: And that quietness is what set Melvin apart immediately,
sentences.zh: 而那种安静正是让梅尔文脱颖而出的原因，

sentences.en: the night he hosted his first show in May 1976.
sentences.zh: 就在他1976年5月主持第一场节目的那个晚上。

sentences.en: That's because Melvin represented a new kind of on-air personality.
sentences.zh: 这是因为梅尔文代表了一种新型的广播个性。

sentences.en: The previous generation of Black radio DJs were super performative,
sentences.zh: 上一代黑人广播DJ非常注重表演，

sentences.en: Rocket ship time one more time, and look out, y'all, cause here we go!
sentences.zh: 火箭飞船时间又到了，大家小心，因为我们要出发了！

sentences.en: Let's continue on with more recorded music.
sentences.zh: 让我们继续播放更多的录制音乐。

sentences.en: Melvin mellowed that profile way out.
sentences.zh: 梅尔文把那种风格完全柔和化了。

sentences.en: When he spoke, oh, pure satin.
sentences.zh: 当他说话时，哦，纯粹的丝绸般顺滑。

sentences.en: Melvin was so gentle and fluid, and it all seemed just effortless.
sentences.zh: 梅尔文是如此温柔和流畅，一切看起来都毫不费力。

sentences.en: The next couple of songs I'm going to play have a lot of meaning for me,
sentences.zh: 接下来我要播放的几首歌对我来说意义重大，

sentences.en: and I want you to listen to the words.
They're dedicated from me to you, and then I'll be back to say something else before I go.
sentences.zh: 它们是我献给你们的，在我离开之前，我会回来再说点别的。

sentences.en: His style of radio, it made you feel like he was talking directly to you.
sentences.zh: 他的广播风格让你觉得他是在直接和你对话。

sentences.en: That's a big achievement, to be able to do that as a radio personality.
sentences.zh: 作为一名电台主持人，能做到这一点是一项了不起的成就。

sentences.en: Like, he prepared this great soul-satisfied meal.
sentences.zh: 他准备了一顿让人心满意足的饕餮盛宴。

sentences.en: Well, WHUR had never done a show that sounded like this.
sentences.zh: 要知道，WHUR电台此前从未做过听起来像这样的节目。

sentences.en: Up to that point, the station was mostly a mix of public affairs programming and a lot of jazz.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，该电台主要播放公共事务节目和大量的爵士乐。
绝对不是那种适合调情的B面情歌。

sentences.en: Listeners were caught totally off guard.
sentences.zh: 听众们完全被打了个措手不及。

sentences.en: On the night of the first broadcast,
sentences.zh: 在首次播出的那天晚上，

sentences.en: Melvin was flooded with calls from people requesting their own favorite slow jaMs.
sentences.zh: 梅尔文接到了无数听众打来的电话，要求点播他们最喜欢的慢歌。

sentences.en: Others phoned in just to show the young DJ some love.
sentences.zh: 还有些人打电话进来，只是为了向这位年轻的DJ表达喜爱。

sentences.en: For the next two days, WHUR's switchboard lit up with listeners calling in from all over the D.C.
sentences.zh: 接下来的两天里，WHUR的电话总机响个不停，来自华盛顿特区各地的听众

sentences.en: area asking about that new show.
Together, Kathy Hughes and Melvin Lindsay, the intern student babysitter, had just created a hit.
sentences.zh: 凯西·休斯和当时还是实习生兼保姆的梅尔文·林赛，就这样共同打造了一个爆款节目。

sentences.en: Here's Melvin in 1991 talking about how the show just took off.
sentences.zh: 这是梅尔文在1991年谈论该节目如何一炮而红的片段。

sentences.en: It started out of love, out of fun, out of people putting their heads together,
sentences.zh: 它源于热爱，源于乐趣，源于大家集思广益，

sentences.en: and not even realizing that we were really creating such a monster, you know, in the radio industry.
sentences.zh: 甚至没意识到我们真的在广播行业创造了一个庞然大物。

sentences.en: But the program still needed a name.
sentences.zh: 但节目当时还没有名字。

sentences.en: About a year before the show first went on the air,
sentences.zh: 在节目开播前大约一年，

The Quiet Storm show started in 1976,
and by the end of the next year,
it was the number one weekend music show in Washington.
